column1: # Game profile of Pokémon Legends: Z-A (Switch, base game v0 + update 2.0.2 = v393216). Plays on the Mac
# Game Freak's Trinity engine on SDK 19.3.11, NVN 55, Havok 2022.2. Every file lives in the Trinity packs of arc/data.trpfs (FlatBuffers, Oodle Mermaid); started from the provisional profile
# the game sets the near=0 depth mode (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode): the pipeline bases made before it runs take the main0_z vertex entries
# nninitStartup (main+0x1b2e650) initializes its StandardAllocator with virtual address memory over 12 GB of address space (StandardAllocator::Initialize(nullptr, 0x300000000), main+0x1b3e3ec),

# which the Switch's 64 GB alias region holds. Two cuts for 2.0.2 (patches.py and dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) make it fit the 5 GB block proven on a phone: the allocator gets 4 GB and the SDK's node area 62 MB instead
# of 1 GB, so the alias region holds 62 MB + 4 GB (SDK 19 puts the region 4 MB aligned right after the node area)
# nninitStartup allocates and frees all it can (pool − 64 MB) and the SDK keeps those pages mapped until a map fails: the pool is enforced as on Horizon, so it gives them back (hle_svc.c)
# Game Freak's Trinity engine: every shader is a BNSH inside the Oodle-compressed packs of arc/data.trpfs (shader_split.py trpfs_jobs), named by the pack's first file:
# the material shaders in system_resource/gfx2/shader, particle effects in ik_effectdata, UI layouts (__ArchiveShader.bnsh in .truiv) in uidata

# The packs are Oodle Mermaid streams; the shader split decodes them with the game's own OodleLZ_Decompress in the Mac host (dm/host/hle_oodle.c), which the NSP script builds for any game with Trinity packs
